rows.template: **Current measured result (R25, staging).** One backend with and without the augmentation,
six arms, seven interleaved repetitions. The shipped planned write (arm C,
`weftfs checkpoint write`, no flags) of the frozen 101-tensor Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct subset
(424,439,296 logical bytes) takes **{{contract.C.ms_min}} ms** least-contended /
**{{contract.C.ms_p50}} ms** p50 on 4 CPUs in the 3 GiB court, and publishes
**{{contract.C.foot_b}} B** — **{{contract.C.storage_pct}} %** fewer physical bytes than the same
backend's native per-tensor path (arm A, **{{contract.A.ms_min}} ms**, {{contract.A.foot_b}} B).
That is **{{contract.C.ratio}}×** the native wall: native parity is not reached. All 101 restores
are byte-exact. The ≈{{frontier.c.ms_min}} ms frontier in
[`bench/RESULTS-pareto.md`](bench/RESULTS-pareto.md) is a store-API row, **not** the shipped
default. Source: `{{contract.C.ms_min|receipt}}` (stamp {{contract.C.ms_min|stamp}},
revision {{contract.C.ms_min|revision}}).
| Question | Result from a receipt | Where |

| Does reconstruction reduce stored bytes? | Qwen2.5-0.5B base → Instruct family: **{{family.total_b}} B** (**{{family.data_b}} B** of tensor data) versus **{{family.independent_zstd_b}} B** for independent per-tensor `zstd -19` (**{{family.zstd_delta_pct}} %** smaller) and **{{family.zipnn_b}} B** for ZipNN 0.5.4 (**{{family.zipnn_delta_pct}} %** under). | `{{family.total_b|receipt}}`, `{{family.independent_zstd_b|receipt}}` (stamp {{family.total_b|stamp}}, revision {{family.total_b|revision}}), [`bench/RESULTS-real-model.md`](bench/RESULTS-real-model.md) |

| Does independent tiling make region reads cheap? | Qwen embedding one-row read: **{{tiles.row1_mode9_ms}} ms** as one mode-9 frame → **{{tiles.row1_tiled_ms}} ms** with tiles (**{{tiles.speedup_row1}}×**), at **+{{tiles.byte_overhead_pct}} %** physical bytes; a 100-row read falls from **{{tiles.row100_mode9_ms}} ms** to **{{tiles.row100_tiled_ms}} ms** (**{{tiles.speedup_row100}}×**). | `{{tiles.row1_mode9_ms|receipt}}` (stamp {{tiles.row1_mode9_ms|stamp}}, revision {{tiles.row1_mode9_ms|revision}}), [`bench/RESULTS-mode17.md`](bench/RESULTS-mode17.md) |

| What exactness and recovery evidence exists? | **{{verify.passed}}/{{verify.courts}}** verification courts pass at parent `{{verify.revision|revision}}` (stamp {{verify.stamp}}); **{{conformance.vectors}}** conformance vectors; **{{crash.requested}}/{{crash.requested}}** crash iterations with **{{crash.bad}}** bad states. | `{{verify.passed|receipt}}`, `conformance/manifest.json`, `{{crash.requested|receipt}}` |

| Does multi-writer publication scale? | **No, and it is published as a loss:** {{mw.n1_tx_s}} tx/s at N=1 → {{mw.n32_tx_s}} tx/s at N=32 (efficiency **{{mw.n32_efficiency}}**) on the local backend; a hot name yields exactly one winner and typed conflicts. MinIO N=4: {{mw.minio_n4_tx_s}} tx/s. | `{{mw.n1_tx_s|receipt}}` (stamp {{mw.n1_tx_s|stamp}}, revision {{mw.n1_tx_s|revision}}), [`bench/RESULTS-multiwriter.md`](bench/RESULTS-multiwriter.md) |

**Implemented** (store core, no FUSE) — the Rust all-targets suite passes: **{{tests.rust_store_passed}}** tests in {{tests.rust_store_binaries}} test-result groups, 0 failed, in the {{verify.passed}}/{{verify.courts}} aggregate; see [`docs/store-status.md`](docs/store-status.md)

**Implemented** — the FUSE all-targets suite passes: **{{tests.rust_fuse_passed}}** passed / {{tests.rust_fuse_failed}} failed / {{tests.rust_fuse_ignored}} `#[ignore]`d in the {{verify.passed}}/{{verify.courts}} aggregate log; ownership needs `CAP_SETUID`, and same-inode direct-I/O concurrency hits a reproducible kernel/fuser EIO. Store-level atomicity is tested separately — see [`docs/fuse-status.md`](docs/fuse-status.md)

**v1.4.1 released** — per-repo GHCR images and crates.io crates, per-repo GitHub releases, and the codec/store/`fio`/FUSE comparative suites exist. Latest full verification: `bench/receipts/verify-{{verify.stamp}}.json` (**{{verify.passed}}/{{verify.courts}}**, {{verify.failed}} failed, {{verify.skipped}} skipped) at parent `{{verify.revision|revision}}`. The authoritative inventory is `scripts/verify-all.sh`. Losses and gaps are published in the `bench/RESULTS-*.md` files listed there; no performance-superiority claim is made. See [`docs/RELEASE-v1.4.1.md`](docs/RELEASE-v1.4.1.md); the previous release note is [`docs/RELEASE-v1.4.0.md`](docs/RELEASE-v1.4.0.md).
- **The compressed write, {{write.speedup_r17}}× faster and still not at native parity.** The
durable write of the 101-tensor fixture goes from **{{ladder.r17_ms}} ms** (R17, where
ZSTD-19 was {{ladder.r17_zstd19_ms}} ms — the largest single term — for zero chosen tensors) to
**{{write.r22.min_ms}} ms** least-contended / {{write.r22.med_ms}} ms median (R22) at an
unchanged **{{write.r22.footprint_b}} B** — {{write.reduction_pct}} % below the native control's
{{write.a.footprint_b}} B. G1/G2/G3 are met; the ≤ 336 ms native rung is **not**
({{write.ratio}}× A), and the measured limiter (the {{write.r22.barrier_ms}} ms durable
writeback of {{write.r22.barrier_files}} files plus a {{write.r22.publish_wall_ms}} ms publication wall) is
stated with the one change most likely to close it. Receipts
`r21-pipeline-20261112T201500Z`; analysis
[`bench/RESULTS-pareto.md`](bench/RESULTS-pareto.md) and
[`bench/RESULTS-write-cost-ledger.md`](bench/RESULTS-write-cost-ledger.md).
- **Checkpoint sessions and a bounded queue (R12c).** A reused
`CheckpointSession` takes warm completion p50 from **{{session.persave_warm_p50_ms}} → {{session.session_warm_p50_ms}} ms** at a
4-step interval; a bounded queue (default 2 outstanding) turns a timing-decided
race into a documented admission bound and cuts the 1-step loop wall
**{{queue.baseline_wall_ms}} → {{queue.bounded_wall_ms}} ms** with 96/96 saves landed and no silent skip. Losses:
completion p95 and RSS get worse and the queue cannot make a save finish
sooner. Receipts `training-goodput-session-20261111T220500Z.json`,
`checkpoint-queue-bound-after-20261112T043000Z.json`.
- **Incremental index and metadata (R12c).** Publish no longer rebuilds the
selector index: commit p50 is **{{index.baseline_commit_p50_ms}} → {{index.post_commit_p50_ms}} ms** at 1k
generations and {{index.post_commit_p50_100k_ms}} ms at 100k, at byte-identical index bytes, with a real GC
defect (one shared retained-chain bound) found and fixed; DCP metadata encoding falls
**{{dcp.reference_p50_ms}} → {{dcp.path_p50_ms}} ms** behind an oracle-checked plan. Analysis
[`bench/RESULTS-incremental-index.md`](bench/RESULTS-incremental-index.md),
[`bench/RESULTS-dcp-metadata.md`](bench/RESULTS-dcp-metadata.md).
- **Azure MW2 verified in both languages (R14d).** MW2 is now available on the
`azure` commit plane in Rust and Go, refused on GCS. The Go half was committed
unverified and its suite failed; the reproduced failure was Go recovery
consulting a stale writer `LOCK` record instead of the `writers` policy, fixed
at one decision point with a regression test for the fail-closed default.
Evidence: `bench/receipts/r14d-go-suite-20261112T221649Z.json`.
- **Verification.** `bench/receipts/verify-{{verify.v140.stamp}}.json` — **{{verify.v140.passed}}/{{verify.v140.courts}}**
courts pass, {{verify.v140.failed}} failed, {{verify.v140.skipped}} skipped, at parent `{{verify.v140.revision|revision}}`
(WeftCodec `d95fa78`, WeftCodec-Go `0db665e`, WeftFS-Go `6d58137`); **{{conformance.vectors}}**
conformance vectors, aggregate `{{conformance.aggregate}}`; **{{claims.count}}** audited claims.
**At a glance (generated from receipts).** v1.4.1 is released. The cited aggregate is
`bench/receipts/verify-{{verify.stamp}}.json` — **{{verify.passed}}/{{verify.courts}}** courts pass,
{{verify.failed}} failed, {{verify.skipped}} skipped — at WeftFS `{{verify.revision}}`.

the native control, {{contract.C.ratio}}× its wall). Rust all-targets

**Current measured result (R25).** One backend with and without the augmentation: the shipped
planned write (arm C, `weftfs checkpoint write`, no flags) of the frozen 101-tensor
Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct subset (424,439,296 logical bytes) takes **{{contract.C.ms_min}} ms**
least-contended and **{{contract.C.ms_p50}} ms** p50 in the 3 GiB / 4-CPU court, and publishes
**{{contract.C.foot_b}} B** — **{{contract.C.storage_pct}} %** fewer physical bytes than the same
backend's native per-tensor path (arm A, **{{contract.A.ms_min}} ms**, {{contract.A.foot_b}} B).
That is **{{contract.C.ratio}}×** the native wall: native parity is **not** reached. Every one of
the 101 restores is byte-exact, and the chosen representations are identical across all
seven interleaved repetitions. Receipt `{{contract.C.ms_min|receipt}}`
(stamp {{contract.C.ms_min|stamp}}, revision {{contract.C.ms_min|revision}}).
The separately measured **frontier** — arm C driven through the bounded prepare/publish
pipeline (`Store::prepare_tensor_group_pipelined`) — is **{{frontier.c.ms_min}} ms**
({{frontier.c.ratio}}× A) at {{frontier.c.foot_b}} B on the same fixture, but no shipped CLI verb
reaches that composition. It is not the default and is not claimed as one (§3.1).
Manifest: **{{conformance.vectors}}** vectors, aggregate
`{{conformance.aggregate}}`; the per-mode distribution is the `modes` object in
`conformance/manifest.json`. Regenerate with
`scripts/gen-conformance-manifest.sh` and check with `--check`;
`scripts/check-conformance-coverage.sh` fails when an allocated mode lacks a
valid and a reject vector.
| Question | Answer |

| Did the compressed write get faster? | **Yes, {{write.speedup_r17}}×**: {{ladder.r17_ms}} ms at R17 to **{{write.r22.min_ms}} ms** least-contended / {{write.r22.med_ms}} ms median at R22, at the same {{write.r22.footprint_b}} B |

| Did it reach native parity? | **No.** The native per-tensor control A is {{write.a.min_ms}}–{{write.a.med_ms}} ms; {{write.r22.min_ms}} ms is **{{write.ratio}}× A**. The ≤ 336 ms rung is **not met**, and the limiter is stated in §6 |
| Did the bytes change? | **No.** Every planned row publishes {{write.r22.footprint_b}} B — **{{write.reduction_pct}} %** below A's {{write.a.footprint_b}} B — and every restores 101/101 exactly |

Two terms account for it:
1. **Encode work that cannot be compressed further at this operating point.**
The encode term is {{write.r22.encode_ms}} ms summed over threads (level 3

**{{write.r22.barrier_files}} files / 282 MB in {{write.r22.barrier_ms}} ms** while native
writes A's {{write.a.footprint_b}} B in {{write.a.min_ms}} ms. The publisher's own wall
is {{write.r22.publish_wall_ms}} ms. The last tensors publish after the last encode, so
the tail is charged in full.
**The one change most likely to close it**, from the measurements: make the
durable state **fewer and larger objects, without a sealing cost on the critical
path**. The pack plane is the right shape and is already measured to cut
publisher busy time from {{write.r22.publish_busy_ms}} ms to {{write.r22.pack_publish_busy_ms}} ms and to
eliminate every writeback file — it loses only because sealing and the catalog
publish are charged to the publisher (total {{write.r22.pack_min_ms}} ms). Moving pack
sealing and the catalog publication onto the early-barrier thread is the
concrete next step.

* **Persistent sessions (item 1).** One `CheckpointSession` per (store, run)
instead of a helper process per checkpoint. Warm completion p50 falls
**{{session.persave_warm_p50_ms}} → {{session.session_warm_p50_ms}} ms** at a 4-step interval; loop wall
{{session.persave_loop_wall_ms}} → **{{session.session_loop_wall_ms}} ms**; training-thread pause p50
{{session.persave_pause_p50_ms}} → **{{session.session_pause_p50_ms}} ms**. Every resumed state and next-step loss bit in
the receipt matched. Receipt `training-goodput-session-20261111T220500Z.json`.
* **Operation-derived incremental index (item 2).** Publish no longer calls
`StateIndex::build`. Commit p50 is **{{index.baseline_commit_p50_ms}} → {{index.post_commit_p50_ms}} ms** at 1k
generations and {{index.post_commit_p50_100k_ms}} ms at 100k — flat while history grows 100× — with
byte-identical index segments; 10k live objects fall
{{index.live10k_baseline_ms}} → **{{index.live10k_post_ms}} ms**. A same-revision control with maintenance disabled
reproduces the baseline. Receipts
`incremental-index-20261111T220000Z-baseline-delta-live64`,
`…T230000Z-post-delta-live64`, `…T235000Z-post-delta-live10000`; analysis
[`bench/RESULTS-incremental-index.md`](../bench/RESULTS-incremental-index.md).
* **Index GC bound per retained root (item 2.1).** Item 2 exposed a real defect:
the retained-chain depth bound was applied to one `visited` set shared by every
root, so index GC refused once several snapshots were retained and the index
tree grew with commits. Fixed per root in both languages; all retained
snapshots still load their full chain. Retained failures:
`index-gc-bound-20261111T190100Z-prefix-8roots.json`, `…T194000Z-prefix-tail.json`.
* **DCP metadata encoding (item 3).** The pure-Python canonical encoder cost
**{{dcp.reference_p50_ms}} ms p50**; a reusable plan plus a fast generic encoder take it to
**{{dcp.path_p50_ms}} ms** warm ({{dcp.plan_match_ms}} ms signature + {{dcp.plan_assemble_ms}} ms assembly), with the
reference encoder kept as the oracle and every plan proved equal to it before
use; the first call pays a {{dcp.path_first_ms}} ms plan build. Receipts
`dcp-metadata-20261111T230500Z.json`, `…T235500Z.json`.
* **Bounded checkpoint queue (item 4).** `CheckpointSession` admits saves under
`max_outstanding` (**default 2**), a staged-byte budget and a blocking wait with
a 30 s ceiling; a refusal is `QueueFull` naming every bound and publishes
nothing. At a 1-step interval the loop wall falls **{{queue.baseline_wall_ms}} → {{queue.bounded_wall_ms}} ms**
({{queue.baseline_warm_p50_ms}} → {{queue.bounded_warm_p50_ms}} ms warm p50, {{queue.bounded_warm_p95_ms}} ms p95), every save lands,
`no_silent_skips` is true and every cell drains to `outstanding 0`. Receipt
`checkpoint-queue-bound-after-20261112T043000Z.json`, baseline
`checkpoint-queue-sweep-baseline-20261112T020000Z.json`.
The R17 wall was dominated by one term: level-19 ZSTD accounted for
{{write.r17_zstd19_share_pct}} % of it ({{ladder.r17_zstd19_ms}} ms) and was selected for **zero** tensors.

We argue a specific, disagreeable thesis:
> **For AI state, the identity of an artifact should be independent of its
> physical representation, and representation choice should be optimised
> against a measured lifecycle cost surface. When this is done, exactness
> and selective reconstruction are affordable — but the surface is not
> globally favourable: on one write-dominated workload the shipped
> augmentation is **{{contract.C.ratio}}×** slower to write for
> **{{contract.C.storage_pct}} %** fewer physical bytes, the same design's
> measured frontier is **{{frontier.c.ratio}}×**, and on a 32-bit
> `FLOAT_TENSOR` workload it is **{{family.pythia0.ratio}}×** slower.**
The first clause is a design constraint, not a performance result. The second
clause is a measurement result, and it is the part we expect a storage engineer
to attack. Our contribution is not a faster store. It is a set of identities,
refusals, and cost terms whose predictions can be checked — and falsified —
from committed artifacts without rerunning our courts. The headline numbers
come from `{{contract.C.ms_min|receipt}}` (stamp {{contract.C.ms_min|stamp}};
revision {{contract.C.ms_min|revision}}), the frontier receipt
`{{frontier.c.ms_min|receipt}}` (stamp {{frontier.c.ms_min|stamp}}; revision
{{frontier.c.ms_min|revision}}), and the pythia receipt
`{{family.pythia0.c_ms|receipt}}` (stamp {{family.pythia0.c_ms|stamp}};
revision {{family.pythia0.c_ms|revision}}). The superseded R3 number is
retained below as history, with its stamp and revision.
**What is compared.** One backend with and without the WeftFS protocol and
codec (arms A native, N native + manifest, B pass-through, C codec, D protocol,
E combined). The Rust/Go reference filesystem is development provenance and is
never the comparator, and no row pits it against another filesystem.
**Measured (R25).** All six arms restored all 101 tensors with `mismatches: 0`;
the physical footprints were {{contract.A.foot_b}} B (A), {{contract.N.foot_b}} B (N),
{{contract.B.foot_b}} B (B), {{contract.C.foot_b}} B (C), {{contract.D.foot_b}} B (D) and
{{contract.E.foot_b}} B (E) for the same 424,439,296 logical bytes. The chosen
representations are identical across all seven repetitions. In the overlay court
(receipt `overlay-20261106T103115Z.json`) the COW run, the overlay run and the
post-compaction run all produced content root `c00367f0…`
**Measured (R25).** On the frozen fixture the shipped planned codec cuts physical
bytes by {{contract.C.storage_pct}} % and raises the durable write wall from
{{contract.A.ms_min}} ms to {{contract.C.ms_min}} ms ({{contract.C.ratio}}×), with
{{contract.C.cpu_ms}} ms of write CPU versus {{contract.A.cpu_ms}} ms for the native
path. A bytes-only comparison calls that a win; a write-aware comparison does not.
